newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs end down on continued political worries.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs end down on continued political worries.

text.p: Share prices on the Lima Stock Exchange fell Wednesday due to continuing political worries following a series of scandals, which have plagued President Alberto Fujimori's government in recent weeks, brokers said.
But they predicted prices would remain broadly stable Thursday, with investors expected to buy shares in construction, mining and brewery sector companies.
The General Index fell 1.75 percent to 2,067.54 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index also fell 1.9 percent to 2,950.33 points, according to preliminary stock exchange figures.
In a total of 2,123 trades, volume was 38.7 million soles ($14.7 million) as 49 stocks fell, 25 remained stable and 15 rose.

"Due to the political situation investors are cautious and are taking refuge in shares that have good perspectives ... and can stand up to any problems," said Carlos Patron of local brokerage Peruval.
Fujimori's popularity in the polls has fallen to its lowest point in his seven years in office after Peruvians have become increasingly hostile to his perceived authoritarian style.

Last week, media allegations of phone tapping by the secret services and the government's attempt to annul the Peruvian citizenship of an Israeli-born television station owner led to violent protests against Fujimori.

Patron said rising zinc prices that boosted the polymetallic mining sector, increasing brewery sales and growth in the construction sector prevented the market from falling further due to the political crisis.
Losers Wednesday included electricity company Edegel, which fell 5.5 percent to 1.03 soles and Banco de Credito, which slipped 2.67 percent to 3.65 soles.
Among shares that bucked the downward trend, benchmark Telefonica del Peru "B" rose 0.63 percent to 6.34 soles and tin miner Minsur climbed 0.61 percent to 8.25 soles.
